mechanism_narrative: Higher federal funds rates compress equity valuations through increased discount rates applied to future cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS is above 4.5% (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that increases equity risk premiums, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS > 5.0 (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When both inflation (CPIAUCSL) and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) are high (CPIAUCSL > 305 and FEDFUNDS > 4.5), it signals a high-risk environment for equities, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both CPIAUCSL > 305 and FEDFUNDS > 4.5 (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high real GDP growth (year-over-year growth rate of GDPC1 > 2%), the S&P 500 forward returns are positive over the next 60 trading days due to sustained economic expansion supporting corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when GDPC1_YOY_growth > 2.0 (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1600 thousand units, it signals strong consumer demand and economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST > 1600 (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 3.5%, it signals a tight labor market that supports wage growth and corporate profitability, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when UNRATE < 3.5 (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) show month-over-month growth above 0.5%, it signals robust economic activity across manufacturing and construction, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both INDPRO_MOM_growth > 0.5 and HOUST_MOM_growth > 0.5 (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 0.5% signals persistent inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to immediate market reaction to inflation data.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL_MOM_growth > 0.5 (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
